The Ashoka rock edicts are a series of inscriptions carved on stone pillars and rocks across the Indian subcontinent by the Mauryan emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE. They are the primary historical source for his reign and his promotion of Dhamma (Dharma), emphasizing non-violence, tolerance, and welfare.
